doc.title: Peter Ecklund interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 14, 1998

title: Bebop's difficulty and which players he likes today
summary: He says bebop is hard and rarely played well, and names Roy Hargrove among younger players he likes.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: talking like the kind of flowering period of jazz in the ‘50s and ‘60s, that’s really a very short time. And it’s also extremely difficult music to play well. I’d say, I mean I like bebop when it’s played well, but it almost never is. It’s really very difficult music. And when you put on one of those great Blue Note albums and then you hear like some modern day group, I think it’s probably, it falls short even more than the efforts of myself and my friends to play old music, it falls short, if for no other reason than the music is more difficult.
Anybody out there you enjoy listening to today?

Oh yeah. Well I like some of the players here. Among the sort of younger generation of players, I think the one I like — I like Roy Hargrove, he’s very good. A lot of them I’m not really that familiar with. You know how it is in music, there’s some things that you recognize that are very good but they just don’t happen to appeal to you.
